A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a high energy π − beam could be bent by a crystal through a channeling and a doughnut scattering.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the deflection of high-energy particles by bent crystals is a promising technique for the production of secondary particle beams with a well-defined energy and momentum.
the crystal bending can be used to deflect the beam in the opposite direction with the efficiency up to 50% and to select particles in quasi-bound states with the probability of 20%.
the deflection of high-energy particles in a bent single crystal is not a unique phenomenon, but can be stimulated in different ways.
